doc: Strength exp(-d / 1200 km) of marine stratocumulus for each ocean cell, d the distance to the next coast cell (cont >= 0.5, tested on the float32 values) DOWNSTREAM along its row (east on a prograde body; the row is mirrored for spin < 0, spin >= 0 counts as prograde), in wrapped columns times dx = 2 pi R / w max(cos lat, 1e-3); d x dx > 4000 km (strict) is infinite (strength 0); the result is multiplied by (1 - cont) (so a coast cell keeps at most 0.5). Rows with no coast or only coast are skipped (zeros). The exp is float64 rounded to float32, then a float32 product. `cont` is a float32 array and the test `cont >= 0.5` is made on those float32 values (0.5 is exact in both precisions): a port must keep cont in float32, because the hand-built inputs below put cells exactly on 0.5 and one float32 ulp either side of it. A 16x4 field with a coast cell in column 10 of every row; the radius is chosen so that, on row 1 (22.5 deg), a distance of 3 columns is 4000 km plus 1e-9 relative: the texels in column 7 there are cut to 0 (infinite distance). The relative margin of 1e-9 is several million float64 ulps (an ulp is 1.1e-16 to 2.2e-16 relative), so a cos or a product that differs in the last ulp does not flip it. Default tolerance (measured 7.5e-8). params.constants lists the module constants and the inline numbers the function reads (a port copies them from its own source and may assert that they equal these).
